cards.name: IVGEffectTwisterDistortion
cards.summary: Settings object of a Twister distortion (Distort tool, Twister mode): its single Angle property sets how far the shape is wound around the distortion centre, turning the outline into a pinwheel / swirl whose arms wrap further the larger the angle.
use_for: swirl and pinwheel ornaments from a star or polygon
twisted logo marks and psychedelic badge backgrounds
re-tuning the twist amount of an existing Twister distortion in a batch
avoid: subtle bends or arcs of text: use an envelope or Fit Text To Path instead
shapes that must keep exact geometry for cutting or CNC: convert the result to curves and check node count first
cards.how: Not created directly. Shape.CreateTwisterDistortion(OriginX, OriginY, Angle) returns an Effect; Effect.Distortion.Twister is this object (an existing one is found through Shape.Effects.DistortionEffects). The centre lives on the parent IVGEffectDistortion (OriginX / OriginY, CenterDistortion).

key_members.name: Angle
key_members.use: total twist in degrees (double); larger values wrap the arms further around the centre

key_members.name: Parent
key_members.use: the IVGEffectDistortion: Type, OriginX / OriginY, CenterDistortion

gotchas: the twist centre is not on this object: move it with Parent.OriginX / OriginY or Parent.CenterDistortion
the UI splits the amount into complete rotations + additional degrees; whether Angle above 360 adds whole turns and a negative Angle reverses the direction is (unverified)
the distortion is live on the control shape: the curve you see is the effect result, and editing the original shape re-runs it (unverified)
a shape with few nodes twists coarsely; add nodes or use a polygon / star with many points for a smooth swirl (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape, eff As Effect
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreatePolygon2(100, 100, 40, 8, , 15, True)
Set eff = s.CreateTwisterDistortion(100, 100, 270)
eff.Distortion.CenterDistortion
eff.Distortion.Twister.Angle = 540

cards.name: IVGEffectZipperDistortion
cards.summary: Settings object of a Zipper distortion (Distort tool, Zipper mode): it adds saw-tooth zigzags along the outline, with Amplitude (tooth height) and Frequency (tooth count) plus Random, Smooth (rounded waves instead of points) and Local (teeth strongest near the distortion centre) switches.
use_for: jagged comic burst and explosion shapes
torn-paper or electric edges on a badge
wavy scalloped borders with Smooth on
rough hand-made edges on a sticker outline
avoid: clean even scallops for a print border: use a polygon / star or Blend instead; Zipper teeth are laid out per segment, so uneven node spacing gives uneven teeth (unverified)
cut contours for a plotter: the result has many nodes; simplify before export
cards.how: Not created directly. Shape.CreateZipperDistortion(OriginX, OriginY, Amplitude, Frequency, Random, Smooth, Local) returns an Effect; Effect.Distortion.Zipper is this object. The centre (which matters for Local) is on the parent IVGEffectDistortion.

key_members.name: Amplitude
key_members.use: tooth height (long); no range in the harvest

key_members.name: Frequency
key_members.use: how many teeth (long); no range in the harvest; teeth appear to be laid out per segment between nodes (unverified)

key_members.name: Random
key_members.use: irregular tooth sizes for a rough, hand-torn edge

key_members.name: Smooth
key_members.use: round the teeth into waves instead of sharp points

key_members.name: Local
key_members.use: teeth strongest near the distortion centre, fading outward

gotchas: Amplitude and Frequency are bare longs with no harvested range; read a value back after setting it rather than assuming the property-bar limits
Local depends on where the distortion centre is (Parent.OriginX / OriginY); a centre outside the shape makes most of the edge flat (unverified)
high Frequency on a small shape gives dense noise and a very heavy curve
the distortion is live: the visible outline is the effect result of the control shape (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape, eff As Effect
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreateEllipse2(100, 100, 50, 50)
Set eff = s.CreateZipperDistortion(100, 100, 40, 12)
eff.Distortion.Zipper.Smooth = False
eff.Distortion.Zipper.Random = True

review.changes: removed the 0-100 Amplitude / Frequency ranges (not in the batch) from key_members and gotchas

cards.name: IVGEllipse
cards.summary: Properties of a native ellipse object (Shape.Type = cdrEllipseShape): whether it is a closed ellipse, an open arc or a pie wedge, its start / end angles and direction, centre and two radii.
use_for: pie-chart wedges and donut-chart segments
arc gauges and progress rings for infographics
resizing circles from data without converting them to curves
badges and seals built from exact circles
avoid: shapes already converted to curves: Shape.Ellipse no longer applies; edit the Curve instead
variable-width rings: use two ellipses combined or a thick outline on an arc
cards.how: Shape.Ellipse on an ellipse shape. Create one with ActiveLayer.CreateEllipse2(CenterX, CenterY, Radius1, Radius2) or CreateEllipse(Left, Top, Right, Bottom); check Shape.Type = cdrEllipseShape before touching .Ellipse.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrEllipseType: cdrEllipse (0) closed, cdrArc (1) open arc, cdrPie (2) wedge

key_members.name: StartAngle
key_members.use: start angle of the arc / pie in degrees

key_members.name: EndAngle
key_members.use: end angle of the arc / pie in degrees

key_members.name: Clockwise
key_members.use: direction the arc runs from StartAngle to EndAngle

key_members.name: SetCenterPosition
key_members.use: move the centre in one call

key_members.name: SetRadius
key_members.use: set both radii (VRadius optional: omit for a circle)

key_members.name: GetRadius
key_members.use: returns both radii through ByRef arguments

gotchas: GetCenterPosition and GetRadius return through ByRef doubles: from VBA pass Double variables; from Python (pywin32) the ByRef values come back as the call's returned tuple, not in the arguments (unverified); reading CenterX / CenterY / HRadius / VRadius is simpler
Shape.Ellipse only exists while the shape is a native ellipse (cdrEllipseShape); after Convert To Curves it fails (unverified)
angles are in degrees; 0 deg pointing to 3 o'clock and counter-clockwise increase is the CorelDRAW convention (unverified)
coordinates use the document unit (ActiveDocument.Unit), not points or pixels
on a rotated or skewed ellipse HRadius / VRadius are the radii before the transform (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreateEllipse2(100, 100, 40, 40)
s.Ellipse.Type = cdrPie
s.Ellipse.StartAngle = 90
s.Ellipse.EndAngle = 210
s.Ellipse.SetRadius 45

review.changes: rewrote the ByRef gotcha: it claimed the values cannot come back from Python / late-bound COM, which is wrong for pywin32 with type info; now hedged

cards.name: IVGEPS
cards.summary: Properties of a placed EPS object (Shape.Type = cdrEPSShape): an EPS imported as a placeable file whose PostScript is kept intact and shown on screen only through its preview bitmap; exposes the PostScript data, the preview, a crop (clipping) envelope, the link path and DCS plate files.
use_for: auditing placed EPS logos in a print file (link path, DCS plates)
pulling the PostScript of a placed EPS for archiving or re-use
resetting a cropped EPS back to its full bounding box
avoid: editing the artwork: the EPS stays a sealed PostScript object; import it as editable (interpreted PostScript) or open it to get curves
screen or web output: only the preview renders on screen; convert it to a bitmap or re-import the file as editable PostScript first
cards.how: Shape.EPS on a placed EPS shape (check Shape.Type = cdrEPSShape first). The object comes from importing an EPS as a placeable file rather than as editable PostScript.

key_members.name: PreviewBitmap
key_members.use: the screen preview bitmap embedded in the EPS

key_members.name: Data
key_members.use: the EPS stream as a byte array

key_members.name: DataAsString
key_members.use: the EPS stream as a string (PostScript text)

key_members.name: CropEnvelope
key_members.use: curve of the current clipping path

key_members.name: CropEnvelopeModified
key_members.use: True when the clip was changed from the original rectangle

key_members.name: BoundingBoxPath
key_members.use: curve of the EPS's original bounding box

key_members.name: LinkFileName
key_members.use: path of the linked EPS file

key_members.name: DCSFileNames
key_members.use: file names of the separation plates of a DCS EPS

gotchas: what shows on screen is PreviewBitmap, not the PostScript: a missing or low-res preview looks wrong on screen but may print correctly
DataAsString on an EPS with a binary preview header (DOS EPS with TIFF / WMF) contains non-text bytes; use Data for an exact copy (unverified)
LinkFileName is harvested as writable although documented as 'Returns'; relinking by setting it is (unverified)
DCSFileNames is empty unless the EPS is a DCS file (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape
For Each s In ActivePage.FindShapes(Type:=cdrEPSShape)
  Debug.Print s.EPS.LinkFileName, s.EPS.CropEnvelopeModified
  If s.EPS.CropEnvelopeModified Then s.EPS.ResetCropEnvelope
Next s

review.changes: avoid: replaced "convert to curves / bitmap" (a placed EPS is not converted to curves) with convert to bitmap or re-import as editable

cards.name: IVGExtrudeVanishingPoint
cards.summary: The vanishing point of an extrude effect: the point the extruded depth recedes toward. Sets whether it is locked to the shape, locked to the page or shared with other extrudes, its X / Y position, and lists the extrudes that share it.
use_for: one consistent perspective across several extruded letters or objects (shared vanishing point)
3D-style headline lettering whose depth points at a chosen spot
batch re-aiming the depth direction of extruded logos
avoid: real 3D renders or materials: extrude is a 2D pseudo-3D effect; use a 3D app or Illustrator's 3D effect
parallel (isometric) extrudes where the depth should not converge: pick a parallel extrude type instead of moving the point (unverified)
cards.how: Effect.Extrude.VanishingPoint, where the Effect comes from Shape.CreateExtrude(Type, VPType, VPX, VPY, ...) or Shape.Effects.ExtrudeEffect on an existing extrude.

key_members.name: Share
key_members.use: share the vanishing point of another extrude (Source); returns True on success

key_members.name: Effects
key_members.use: the extrude effects that share this vanishing point

gotchas: with cdrVPLockedToShape the point moves with the shape, so PositionX / PositionY may be measured relative to the shape rather than the page (unverified)
cdrVPShared is reached by calling Share(Source) with another extrude; assigning Type = cdrVPShared directly is (unverified)
on the parallel extrude types (cdrExtrudeBackParallel / cdrExtrudeFrontParallel) the point sets the depth direction, not a convergence point (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim a As Shape, b As Shape, ea As Effect, eb As Effect
Set a = ActivePage.FindShape("Letter1"): Set b = ActivePage.FindShape("Letter2")
Set ea = a.CreateExtrude(cdrExtrudeSmallBack, cdrVPLockedToPage, 150, 300)
Set eb = b.CreateExtrude(cdrExtrudeSmallBack, cdrVPLockedToPage, 150, 300)
eb.Extrude.VanishingPoint.Share ea.Extrude
Debug.Print ea.Extrude.VanishingPoint.Effects.Count

cards.name: IVGFill
cards.summary: The fill of a shape, text range, text frame, table cell or font properties: reports the fill type and applies or reads uniform, fountain (gradient), pattern, texture, PostScript and hatch fills, or removes the fill.
use_for: brand-colour fills on generated shapes and text
applying gradients, patterns and hatch fills in a batch
copying one object's fill to many (GetCopy / CopyAssign)
checking which fill type an object carries before export
avoid: outlines / strokes: that is Shape.Outline
whole-object transparency: use Shape.Transparency (fountain fills also carry per-node Opacity, see FountainColor)
unattended runs: UserAssign opens a modal fill dialog
cards.how: Shape.Fill (also TextRange.Fill, TextFrame.Fill, table Cell.Fill). An unattached fill comes from Document.CreateFill / CreateUniformFill or Fill.GetCopy and is applied with CopyAssign.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: read-only cdrFillType: cdrNoFill 0, cdrUniformFill 1, cdrFountainFill 2, cdrPostscriptFill 3, cdrTextureFill 8, cdrPatternFill 9, cdrHatchFill 10

key_members.name: UniformColor
key_members.use: the solid colour of a uniform fill

key_members.name: ApplyFountainFill
key_members.use: gradient: start / end colour, type, angle, steps, edge pad, midpoint, blend type, centre offset; returns the FountainFill

key_members.name: Fountain
key_members.use: the FountainFill of a fountain-filled object

key_members.name: ApplyTextureFill
key_members.use: texture from a texture library by name

key_members.name: ApplyPostscriptFill
key_members.use: PostScript fill by index or name

key_members.name: ApplyHatchFill
key_members.use: preset hatch from a hatch library

key_members.name: ApplyCustomHatchFill
key_members.use: hatch built from angle, spacing, line width and colour

key_members.name: Hatch
key_members.use: the HatchFill of a hatch-filled object

key_members.name: CopyAssign
key_members.use: copy another fill's properties onto this one

key_members.name: CompareWith
key_members.use: True when two fills are the same

key_members.name: UserAssign
key_members.use: opens the fill dialog for the user (modal)

gotchas: Type is read-only: change the kind of fill with an Apply* method, not by assignment
reading Fountain / Pattern / Texture / Hatch on a fill of another type gives nothing usable or raises an error; test Type first (unverified)
setting UniformColor on a shape that has no fill may not turn the fill on; call ApplyUniformFill (unverified)
GetCopy is detached: edits to it do not reach the shape until you CopyAssign it back
UserAssign shows a modal dialog and blocks the COM call until a person closes it
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape, t As Shape
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreateRectangle2(0, 0, 100, 60)
s.Fill.ApplyUniformFill CreateRGBColor(230, 57, 70)
If s.Fill.Type = cdrUniformFill Then Debug.Print s.Fill.UniformColor.HexValue
Set t = ActiveLayer.CreateEllipse2(150, 30, 30)
t.Fill.CopyAssign s.Fill

review.changes: summary: dropped "callout" (no callout class has a Fill in the harvest), added font properties (IVGStructFontProperties.Fill); avoid: transparency line no longer denies per-node fountain opacity

cards.name: IVGFillMetadata
cards.summary: Descriptive metadata for a fill saved to or loaded from a fill file: title, description, keywords, subject, copyright and category (each a multi-language string), plus read-only creator tool, creation / modification dates and document / instance IDs.
use_for: tagging fills saved into a shared fill library so they can be searched
reading the title / copyright of a fill file before using it in client work
avoid: document-level metadata (title, keywords of the .cdr): that is Document metadata, not this object
cards.how: Created with Application.CreateFillMetadata, filled in, then passed to StyleFill.SaveFill(FileName, Metadata); StyleFill.LoadFill(FileName, Metadata) reads it back. StyleFill comes from Shape.Style.Fill.

key_members.name: CreatorTool
key_members.use: read-only: application that made the fill file

key_members.name: DocumentID
key_members.use: read-only: ID shared by the fill and its derivatives

key_members.name: InstanceID
key_members.use: read-only: ID of this fill file instance

key_members.name: DerivedFrom
key_members.use: read-only: IDs of the fills this one is derived from

gotchas: the text properties are read-only object references: write the text through them (Title.DefaultLangString = ...), not by assigning Title
CreatorTool, dates and IDs are read-only; they are presumably stamped when the fill file is saved (unverified)
which fill types SaveFill accepts (fountain, pattern, texture, hatch) is (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim md As FillMetadata, s As Shape
Set s = ActiveShape
Set md = CreateFillMetadata
md.Title.DefaultLangString = "Sunset gradient"
md.Keywords.DefaultLangString = "orange, warm, sky"
s.Style.Fill.SaveFill "C:\fills\sunset.fill", md

cards.name: IVGFontList
cards.summary: Read-only list of the font names CorelDRAW knows about (Application.FontList): a 1-based collection of strings with Count and For Each support.
use_for: checking a brand or Devanagari font is installed before building text
picking a fallback font in an automated layout
logging the fonts available on a render machine
avoid: font details such as styles, foundry or file path: this list only gives names
installing fonts: install them in Windows, then call Application.ForceUpdateFontTable to refresh the list
cards.how: Application.FontList; loop with For Each or Item(1..Count). Each item is a font name string.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of fonts in the list

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: enables For Each over the names

gotchas: Item is 1-based and returns a name string, not a font object
fonts installed while CorelDRAW is running can be missing until Application.ForceUpdateFontTable is called (the harvest describes it as picking up newly installed fonts immediately)
names are the family names CorelDRAW shows in its font list; match them case-insensitively and expect style variants to be folded in (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim f As Variant, found As Boolean
For Each f In FontList
  If LCase(f) = "noto sans devanagari" Then found = True
Next f
Debug.Print FontList.Count, found

review.changes: ForceUpdateFontTable gotcha no longer marked unverified (the harvest describes it); avoid names the refresh call

cards.name: IVGFountainColor
cards.summary: One colour node of a fountain fill (gradient stop): its position along the gradient, colour, opacity, the midpoint toward the next node and the blend type used from it.
use_for: recolouring gradient stops to brand colours in a batch
adding fade-to-transparent stops for glows and overlays (Opacity)
moving stops to tighten or widen a colour band
avoid: changing the whole gradient type, angle or spread: that is the parent FountainFill
cards.how: FountainFill.Colors(i), Colors.First or Colors.Last, where FountainFill is Shape.Fill.Fountain (or Shape.Transparency.Fountain).

key_members.name: Color
key_members.use: the node colour (read / assign a Color)

key_members.name: Position
key_members.use: read-only node position along the gradient (long; the scale is not in the harvest, read a node back)

key_members.name: Move
key_members.use: move the node to a new position

key_members.name: MidPoint
key_members.use: midpoint position between this node and the next

key_members.name: BlendType
key_members.use: cdrFountainFillBlendType from this node: direct, rainbow CW / CCW, custom

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: remove the node from the gradient

gotchas: Position is read-only: use Move(NewPosition)
the first and last nodes are the gradient ends and cannot be deleted or moved away from the ends (unverified)
Opacity is a byte: whether 255 or 100 means fully opaque is (unverified); read a node back after setting it
edit a node's colour in place with Color.RGBAssign / CMYKAssign; whether assigning a Color object to Color copies it or keeps a link is (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim ff As FountainFill
Set ff = ActiveShape.Fill.Fountain
ff.Colors.First.Color.RGBAssign 255, 120, 0
ff.Colors.Last.Color.RGBAssign 90, 0, 140
ff.Colors.First.MidPoint = 35

review.changes: Position: removed the "0-100 in the UI" range (not in the batch)

cards.name: IVGFountainColors
cards.summary: The node list of a fountain fill or fountain transparency: count, indexed access to each colour node, the first (start) and last (end) nodes, and Add / AddGrayLevel to insert new nodes at a position.
use_for: building multi-stop gradients (sunset, chrome, rainbow) from code
reading every stop of a gradient to recolour it
grey-level stops for a fountain transparency fade
avoid: setting the gradient type, angle or spread: use the parent FountainFill
cards.how: FountainFill.Colors, where FountainFill is Shape.Fill.Fountain, the result of Fill.ApplyFountainFill, or Shape.Transparency.Fountain.

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: insert a node with a Color at a Position

key_members.name: AddGrayLevel
key_members.use: insert a grey-level node (presumably for fountain transparency, unverified)

key_members.name: GrayLevel
key_members.use: grey level of a node by index

gotchas: Item is documented as base 1, but older CorelDRAW versions counted only the middle nodes and addressed the start as 0 and the end as Count + 1; use First / Last for the ends (unverified)
Add's Position is a long whose scale is not in the harvest; read First.Position / Last.Position to learn it before adding nodes (unverified)
GrayLevel / AddGrayLevel are presumably for fountain transparencies, where nodes are grey levels rather than colours (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim ff As FountainFill
Set ff = ActiveShape.Fill.ApplyFountainFill(CreateRGBColor(255, 200, 0), CreateRGBColor(200, 0, 80))
ff.Colors.Add CreateRGBColor(255, 90, 0), 45
ff.Colors.Add CreateRGBColor(120, 0, 120), 80
Debug.Print ff.Colors.Count

review.changes: removed the 0-100 Position scale (not in the batch); marked the transparency reading of GrayLevel / AddGrayLevel as unverified

cards.name: IVGFountainFill
cards.summary: A fountain (gradient) fill or fountain transparency: linear, radial, conical or square type, its start / end handles, angle, colour nodes, steps, edge pad, midpoint, blend type, spread (pad / reflect / repeat), scale, skew, smooth blending and per-node transparency.
use_for: brand gradients on backgrounds, buttons and lettering
radial glows and spotlights
conical metallic / chrome effects
repeating or reflected gradient stripes (SpreadMethod)
fade-out masks via a fountain transparency
avoid: mesh-like free-form colour blending: use the Mesh Fill tool
gradients along a stroke: CorelDRAW fountain fills fill the interior only
cards.how: Shape.Fill.ApplyFountainFill(StartColor, EndColor, Type, Angle, Steps, EdgePad, MidPoint, BlendType, CenterOffsetX, CenterOffsetY) returns it; Shape.Fill.Fountain reads an existing one; Shape.Transparency.Fountain is the transparency version.

key_members.name: SetAngle
key_members.use: set the gradient angle (Angle is read-only)

key_members.name: SpreadMethod
key_members.use: pad (0), reflect (1) or repeat (2) beyond the handles

key_members.name: SetEdgePad
key_members.use: set the edge pad (EdgePad is read-only)

key_members.name: CenterOffsetX
key_members.use: radial / conical centre offset, % of object width

key_members.name: CenterOffsetY
key_members.use: radial / conical centre offset, % of object height

gotchas: Angle and EdgePad are read-only even though EdgePad's description says 'sets': use SetAngle / SetEdgePad
there is no elliptical enum value; an elliptical gradient is a radial one with Anisotropic / End2X / End2Y set (unverified)
Steps controls banding: a low value gives visible stripes; ApplyFountainFill's default Steps of 0 means the default smooth setting (unverified)
GetTransformations returns through ByRef doubles: from Python (pywin32) the ByRef values come back as the call's returned tuple, not in the arguments (unverified)
the same object type is returned by Shape.Transparency.Fountain; there the nodes act as transparency levels rather than visible colours (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape, ff As FountainFill
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreateRectangle2(0, 0, 210, 297)
Set ff = s.Fill.ApplyFountainFill(CreateRGBColor(255, 90, 0), CreateRGBColor(110, 0, 160), cdrLinearFountainFill, 90)
ff.Colors.Add CreateRGBColor(255, 210, 0), 40
ff.SpreadMethod = cdrFountainFillSpreadMethodReflect
ff.SetAngle 60

review.changes: GetTransformations gotcha claimed Python cannot read ByRef values (wrong for pywin32 with type info), now hedged; transparency-node gotcha marked unverified

cards.name: IVGGMSMacro
cards.summary: One macro (public Sub) inside a loaded GMS (VBA) module: its name plus Run, Edit (opens the VBA editor) and Delete (removes the Sub from the module).
use_for: running a known pipeline macro by name from an outside script
listing a module's macros to check an install
avoid: passing arguments or getting a return value: use GMSManager.RunMacro
unattended runs: Edit opens the VBA editor and Delete changes the module's code
cards.how: Application.GMSManager.Projects("<module>").Macros("<name or index>").

key_members.name: Edit
key_members.use: open the VBA editor at this macro

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: delete the Sub from the module's code

gotchas: Delete removes the code itself, not a shortcut: the module becomes Dirty and the Sub is gone once saved
Run takes no parameters; to pass arguments use GMSManager.RunMacro(ModuleName, MacroName, Parameters)
a macro that opens a form or MsgBox blocks the calling COM call until a person answers it
needs the VBA component of CorelDRAW installed; without it the GMS collections are empty or fail (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim m As GMSMacro
For Each m In GMSManager.Projects("PipelineTools").Macros
  Debug.Print m.Name
Next m
GMSManager.Projects("PipelineTools").Macros("BuildPoster").Run

cards.name: IVGGMSMacros
cards.summary: The macros of one GMS (VBA) module: Count, lookup by index or name, For Each, and Create to add a new empty macro.
use_for: checking a pipeline module exposes the macro a runner expects
listing available macros for a menu or log
avoid: running with arguments: use GMSManager.RunMacro
cards.how: GMSProject.Macros, e.g. Application.GMSManager.Projects("<module>").Macros.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of macros in the module

key_members.name: Create
key_members.use: add a new empty macro (Sub) with a name

gotchas: only parameterless public Subs are expected to appear, like the Macros dialog (unverified)
Create edits the module's source: the project becomes Dirty and is saved on exit (unverified)
a locked or password-protected module may not list its macros (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim p As GMSProject
Set p = GMSManager.Projects("PipelineTools")
Debug.Print p.Macros.Count
If p.Macros.Count > 0 Then Debug.Print p.Macros(1).Name

cards.name: IVGGMSManager
cards.summary: Entry point to CorelDRAW's VBA macro modules (GMS files): the shared and per-user GMS folders, the collection of loaded modules, and RunMacro, which runs a macro with arguments and returns its result.
use_for: driving a heavy VBA macro from an outside pipeline (Python COM) with arguments
installing / locating a pipeline's .gms module
running house macros (imposition, export presets) in batch
avoid: simple object edits that the COM object model can do directly: calling them from the pipeline avoids VBA entirely
cards.how: Application.GMSManager.

key_members.name: RunMacro
key_members.use: run a macro in a GMS module with an array of parameters; returns a variant

key_members.name: UserGMSPath
key_members.use: the GMS folder in the user profile

gotchas: RunMacro is usually called as RunMacro("<GMS project>", "<Module>.<Sub>", Array(...)): the second argument includes the code module name (unverified)
Parameters is a ByRef SAFEARRAY of variants and not optional: pass an empty Array() when the macro takes none; from Python a tuple or list should marshal to it (unverified)
RunMacro blocks until the macro returns; a MsgBox, form or modal dialog inside it hangs the COM caller
a module copied into GMSPath / UserGMSPath is only picked up on the next start unless it is loaded with Projects.Load (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim r As Variant
Debug.Print GMSManager.UserGMSPath
r = GMSManager.RunMacro("PipelineTools", "Module1.BuildPoster", Array("C:\jobs\poster.json", 300))
Debug.Print r

review.changes: Parameters gotcha: the Python tuple claim is now marked unverified and notes the argument is ByRef / required

cards.name: IVGGMSProject
cards.summary: One loaded GMS (VBA project) module: its name, display name, file location, macros, dirty / locked / password flags, and Unload to drop it from memory.
use_for: checking which file a pipeline module was loaded from
unloading a module before replacing its .gms file
detecting locked or password-protected modules before scripting them
avoid: deleting the module file: Unload only removes it from memory
cards.how: GMSManager.Projects("<name or index>"), or the result of Projects.Load / Projects.Create.

key_members.name: DisplayName
key_members.use: name shown in the VBA editor

gotchas: Unload does not delete the .gms file; it is loaded again on the next start if it sits in a GMS folder (unverified)
setting Dirty = False does not save anything; it only clears the flag (unverified)
Locked / PasswordProtected modules can be run but not read or edited (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim p As GMSProject
For Each p In GMSManager.Projects
  Debug.Print p.Name, p.FullFileName, p.Locked
Next p

cards.name: IVGGMSProjects
cards.summary: The collection of loaded GMS (VBA) modules: Count, lookup by index or name, For Each, Load to load a .gms file, and Create to make a new empty module.
use_for: loading a pipeline's .gms at run time before calling RunMacro
checking a module is installed
creating a scratch module for generated macros
avoid: running code: use GMSManager.RunMacro or GMSMacro.Run once the module is loaded
cards.how: Application.GMSManager.Projects.

key_members.name: Load
key_members.use: load a .gms file (CopyFile copies it into the GMS folder, ForAllUsers picks the shared folder)

key_members.name: Create
key_members.use: create a new empty module, optionally for all users

gotchas: Item by name raises an error when the module is not loaded; loop with For Each to test first (unverified)
Load with CopyFile = True copies the file into the GMS folder so it also loads on later starts (unverified)
ForAllUsers writes to the shared GMS folder under Program Files, which needs write rights there (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim p As GMSProject
Set p = GMSManager.Projects.Load("E:\tools\PipelineTools.gms", False)
Debug.Print GMSManager.Projects.Count, p.Name

cards.name: IVGGrid
cards.summary: The document grid: whether it is visible, dot or line style, whether objects snap to it, and its spacing / frequency.
use_for: setting a modular layout grid before interactive design work
a print or pixel grid for icon and signage layouts
turning the grid off before taking previews
avoid: guides at specific positions: create guidelines instead
positioning scripted objects: script coordinates are exact and do not need snapping
cards.how: ActiveDocument.Grid (one grid per document).

key_members.name: Snap
key_members.use: snap objects to the grid while drawing / moving

key_members.name: SetFrequency
key_members.use: set grid lines per unit horizontally and vertically

gotchas: frequency (lines per unit) and spacing (distance between lines) are two views of the same setting; set one of them (unverified)
SetFrequency is described as 'gets or sets' but is a method that only sets
spacing is in document units (ActiveDocument.Unit) (unverified)
Snap only affects interactive drawing; coordinates passed to Create* calls are not snapped (unverified)
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.Grid
  .Type = cdrGridLine
  .SpacingX = 5
  .SpacingY = 5
  .Snap = True
  .Visible = True
End With

cards.name: IVGGuide
cards.summary: A guideline object (Shape.Type = cdrGuidelineShape): horizontal, vertical or slanted, with read-only points, angle and page-centre intercepts, and SetPoints / SetPointAndAngle to move or rotate it.
use_for: bleed, margin and safe-area guides on print templates
column guides for a layout grid
slanted guides for angled typography
avoid: a full regular grid: use the document Grid
visible lines in the artwork: guides do not print, draw lines instead
cards.how: Shape.Guide on a guideline shape. Create guides with Layer.CreateGuide(x1, y1, x2, y2) or Layer.CreateGuideAngle(x, y, Angle), usually on ActivePage.GuidesLayer; find them with GuidesLayer.Shapes.

key_members.name: SetPointAndAngle
key_members.use: move / rotate by a point and slope angle

key_members.name: Preset
key_members.use: read-only: guide comes from a guideline preset

key_members.name: MakeEditable
key_members.use: turn a preset guide into an editable one

key_members.name: InterceptX
key_members.use: X where it crosses the horizontal axis through the page centre

key_members.name: InterceptY
key_members.use: Y where it crosses the vertical axis through the page centre

key_members.name: CenterX
key_members.use: X of the guide point closest to the page centre

key_members.name: CenterY
key_members.use: Y of the guide point closest to the page centre

gotchas: all position properties are read-only: move a guide with SetPoints or SetPointAndAngle

GetPoints / GetPointAndAngle return through ByRef arguments: from Python (pywin32) the ByRef values come back as the call's returned tuple, not in the arguments (unverified); reading Point1X..Point2Y is simpler
preset guides must be made editable (MakeEditable) before they can be moved (unverified)
guides on the master page's guides layer show on every page; ones on a page's GuidesLayer show only there (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim g As Shape
Set g = ActivePage.GuidesLayer.CreateGuide(0, 3, 100, 3)
Debug.Print g.Guide.Type, g.Guide.Point1Y
g.Guide.SetPointAndAngle 50, 10, 0

review.changes: ByRef gotcha claimed the values are unreadable from Python / late-bound COM (wrong for pywin32 with type info); now hedged

cards.name: IVGHatchFill
cards.summary: A hatch fill: one or more sets of parallel lines (each an IVGHatchPattern with angle, spacing, shift, origin and line style) over an optional background colour, with overall scale, rotation and skew; can come from a hatch library or be built line set by line set.
use_for: cross-hatching and section patterns for technical and architectural drawings
engraving / woodcut-style shading on illustrations
line-pattern backgrounds that stay vector and print crisply
laser-engraving and plotter line fills
avoid: photo or texture looks: use a bitmap pattern or texture fill
very fine spacing on large areas: huge line counts slow redraw and export (unverified)
cards.how: Shape.Fill.ApplyHatchFill(LibraryName, HatchNameOrIndex, ...) for a library hatch, Shape.Fill.ApplyCustomHatchFill(Angle, Spacing, ...) for a custom one (both return this object), or Shape.Fill.Hatch on an existing hatch fill.

key_members.name: Patterns
key_members.use: the line sets of the hatch

key_members.name: AddPattern
key_members.use: add a line set: angle, spacing, shift, origin, width, colour, style, dash length, pen width

key_members.name: HasBackground
key_members.use: read-only: hatch has an opaque background

key_members.name: RotationAngle
key_members.use: extra rotation of the whole hatch

key_members.name: SkewAngle
key_members.use: extra skew of the whole hatch

key_members.name: TransformWithShape
key_members.use: hatch scales / rotates with the object

key_members.name: ScaleLinesWithShape
key_members.use: line thickness scales with the object

key_members.name: UseWorldCoordinates
key_members.use: align hatches across separate objects so lines continue

key_members.name: Select
key_members.use: switch to another hatch from a library

key_members.name: AddToLibrary
key_members.use: save this hatch into a library

key_members.name: HatchName
key_members.use: read-only: its name in the library

gotchas: BackColor = Nothing means no background; SetNoBackColor does the same without needing a Nothing assignment from Python
turn UseWorldCoordinates on when several touching objects must share one continuous hatch
spacing and widths are in document units, and how Width differs from PenWidth in AddPattern is (unverified)
IsFromLibrary turns False as soon as any setting is changed, so LibraryName / HatchName then describe only the origin
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape, h As HatchFill
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreateRectangle2(0, 0, 80, 50)
Set h = s.Fill.ApplyCustomHatchFill(45, 3)
h.AddPattern -45, 3
h.SetNoBackColor
h.UseWorldCoordinates = True

cards.name: IVGHatchFills
cards.summary: The hatch fills stored in one hatch library: Count, lookup by name or index, For Each and Find; each item is returned as a general Fill object.
use_for: listing the hatches a library offers
finding a named hatch before applying it
avoid: applying a hatch directly: use Shape.Fill.ApplyHatchFill(LibraryName, HatchNameOrIndex)
cards.how: HatchLibrary.Fills, e.g. ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries.DefaultLibrary.Fills.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of hatches in the library

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: hatch by name or index, returned as a Fill

key_members.name: Find
key_members.use: hatch by name; Nothing when missing

gotchas: items come back as Fill, not HatchFill: read Fill.Hatch for the hatch properties
Find returns Nothing instead of raising an error; Item with a missing name raises (unverified)
the parent HatchLibrary.Fills is described as 'returns the number of hatch fills' but returns this collection
cards.example:
Dim f As Fill
For Each f In ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries.DefaultLibrary.Fills
  Debug.Print f.Hatch.HatchName
Next f

cards.name: IVGHatchLibraries
cards.summary: All hatch-fill libraries available to a document: Count, lookup by name or index, Find, For Each, plus the default library and the last-selected (active) one.
use_for: discovering library names to pass to ApplyHatchFill
picking the default hatch library in a template script
avoid: applying hatches: use Shape.Fill.ApplyHatchFill
cards.how: ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries.

key_members.name: Find
key_members.use: library by name; Nothing when missing

key_members.name: ActiveLibrary
key_members.use: the library last selected in the UI

gotchas: ActiveLibrary follows the UI's last choice, so it differs between machines and sessions; scripts should name the library
match on HatchLibrary.Name (English) rather than DisplayName (translated) for scripts that run on localised installs (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim lib As HatchLibrary
For Each lib In ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries
  Debug.Print lib.Name, lib.Fills.Count
Next lib
Debug.Print ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries.DefaultLibrary.Name

cards.name: IVGHatchLibrary
cards.summary: One hatch-fill library: its English and translated names, its hatch fills, index, whether it is active in the UI, and Activate to make it the active library.
use_for: reading the library name to pass to ApplyHatchFill
browsing a library's hatches
avoid: applying a hatch: use Shape.Fill.ApplyHatchFill with this library's Name
cards.how: ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries("<name or index>"), DefaultLibrary / ActiveLibrary, or HatchFill.Library.

key_members.name: DisplayName
key_members.use: translated name shown in the UI

key_members.name: Fills
key_members.use: the hatch fills in this library

key_members.name: Active
key_members.use: read-only: library is active in the UI

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: make it the active library in the UI

gotchas: Fills is described as 'the number of hatch fills' but returns the HatchFills collection
Activate only changes the UI selection; it does not apply anything to the selection (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim lib As HatchLibrary
Set lib = ActiveDocument.HatchLibraries.DefaultLibrary
ActiveShape.Fill.ApplyHatchFill lib.Name, 1

cards.name: IVGHatchPattern
cards.summary: One set of parallel lines inside a hatch fill: line angle, spacing, origin, shift (absolute or as a percent of the dash length) and the line's outline (width, colour, dash style), with SetProperties for several at once and Reset to defaults.
use_for: tuning cross-hatch density and angle for shading
dashed or coloured hatch lines for technical legends
offsetting line sets to build brick or herringbone-style hatches
avoid: adding a line set: that is HatchFill.AddPattern
solid colour areas: use a uniform fill
cards.how: HatchFill.Patterns(i) or the result of HatchFill.AddPattern(...), where HatchFill is Shape.Fill.Hatch.

key_members.name: Shift
key_members.use: extra sideways shift of successive lines

key_members.name: ShiftPercent
key_members.use: the shift as a percent of the dash-dot length

key_members.name: OriginX
key_members.use: horizontal start of the first line

key_members.name: OriginY
key_members.use: vertical start of the first line

key_members.name: Outline
key_members.use: line properties: width, colour, dash style (read-only reference, edit through it)

key_members.name: SetProperties
key_members.use: set angle, spacing, shift, origin, width, colour, style, dash length and pen width in one call

key_members.name: Reset
key_members.use: reset this line set to defaults

gotchas: Outline is a read-only reference: change the line through it (Outline.Width, Outline.Color), not by assigning a new Outline
GetOrigin returns through ByRef arguments; read OriginX / OriginY from late-bound COM or Python
Shift only shows on dashed lines: on solid lines a sideways shift does not change the look (unverified)
Spacing is in document units (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim p As HatchPattern
Set p = ActiveShape.Fill.Hatch.Patterns(1)
p.Angle = 30
p.Spacing = 2.5
p.Outline.Width = 0.25
p.Outline.Color.RGBAssign 40, 40, 40

cards.name: IVGHatchPatterns
cards.summary: The line sets of one hatch fill: Count, indexed access, For Each, and Reset, which removes all but one line set and resets it to defaults.
use_for: looping over every line set to restyle a hatch
clearing a hatch back to one simple line set before rebuilding it
avoid: adding line sets: use HatchFill.AddPattern
cards.how: HatchFill.Patterns, where HatchFill is Shape.Fill.Hatch.

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: For Each over the line sets

key_members.name: Reset
key_members.use: keep one line set and reset it to defaults

gotchas: Reset is destructive: every line set but one is deleted
Item's index base is not stated in the harvest; HatchPattern.Index tells you the number a set reports (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim p As HatchPattern
For Each p In ActiveShape.Fill.Hatch.Patterns
  p.Outline.Width = 0.2
Next p

cards.name: IVGImage
cards.summary: Raw pixel image behind a bitmap object (or created in memory): colour mode, width / height in pixels, per-pixel colour, tile access to the raw bytes, and Blit / FillArea / FlipArea to draw into it.
use_for: generating procedural textures, noise or pixel art and placing them as bitmaps
sampling colours from a placed photo to build a palette
compositing bitmaps in memory before placing them
building an alpha mask for a generated bitmap
avoid: photo editing (levels, blur, retouching): use the bitmap effects or Photoshop
per-pixel loops over large images through Pixel: read Tiles(i).PixelData in bulk
cards.how: Shape.Bitmap.Image (colour) or Shape.Bitmap.ImageAlpha (transparency) of a bitmap shape; a new one from ActiveDocument.CreateImage(ImageType, Width, Height, FillColor). Place one with Layer.CreateBitmap / CreateBitmap2 / CreateBitmapRect, or write back into a bitmap with Bitmap.SetImageData.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: read-only cdrImageType colour mode (e.g. cdrRGBColorImage 4, cdrCMYKColorImage 5)

key_members.name: Pixel
key_members.use: colour of one pixel (x, y), read-only

key_members.name: Tiles
key_members.use: tiles of raw pixel bytes for bulk read / write

key_members.name: Blit
key_members.use: copy (and scale) a rectangle from another image, with optional merge mode

key_members.name: FillArea
key_members.use: fill a rectangle with a colour

key_members.name: FlipArea
key_members.use: flip a rectangle horizontally, vertically or both

gotchas: the image of an existing bitmap may be ReadOnly: edit GetCopy and write it back with Bitmap.SetImageData (unverified)
Pixel is one COM call per pixel and very slow; read and write Tiles(i).PixelData instead
coordinates are pixels; whether y = 0 is the top row is (unverified)
colour and alpha are separate images (Bitmap.Image and Bitmap.ImageAlpha)
cards.example:
Dim img As Image, s As Shape
Set img = ActiveDocument.CreateImage(cdrRGBColorImage, 256, 256, CreateRGBColor(255, 255, 255))
img.FillArea 0, 0, 128, 128, CreateRGBColor(230, 57, 70)
img.FillArea 128, 128, 128, 128, CreateRGBColor(29, 53, 87)
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreateBitmap2(0, 0, 50, 50, img)

cards.name: IVGImageTile
cards.summary: One rectangular tile of an image's raw pixel memory: its bounds in the image, size, byte layout (bytes per pixel, per line, per tile) and the pixel bytes themselves, readable and (unless read-only) writable as a byte array.
use_for: fast bulk reading of bitmap pixels (colour sampling, histograms)
fast bulk writing of generated pixels (noise, gradients, halftone dots)
avoid: single-pixel lookups: Image.Pixel is simpler
images marked ReadOnly: write into a GetCopy instead
cards.how: Image.Tiles(i), Tiles.First / Tiles.Last, where Image is Shape.Bitmap.Image or ActiveDocument.CreateImage(...).

key_members.name: PixelData
key_members.use: the tile's raw pixel bytes (read / write as a byte array)

key_members.name: BytesPerPixel
key_members.use: bytes per pixel; use it with BytesPerLine to index PixelData

key_members.name: BytesPerLine
key_members.use: bytes per row of the tile, including any padding

gotchas: index rows with BytesPerLine, not Width * BytesPerPixel: rows can be padded (unverified)
PixelData returns a copy: change the array and assign it back (tile.PixelData = arr) for the change to land (unverified)
the channel order inside a pixel (RGB vs BGR) is not in the harvest (unverified)
a big image is split into several tiles; loop over all of Image.Tiles rather than assuming one
cards.example:
Dim img As Image, t As ImageTile, b() As Byte, i As Long
Set img = ActiveShape.Bitmap.Image.GetCopy
For Each t In img.Tiles
  b = t.PixelData
  For i = 0 To UBound(b): b(i) = 255 - b(i): Next i
  t.PixelData = b
Next t
ActiveShape.Bitmap.SetImageData img

review.changes: BytesPerPixel: removed the invented "e.g. 3 for RGB" value

cards.name: IVGImageTiles
cards.summary: The tiles that make up an image's pixel memory: Count, indexed access, For Each, and the first and last tile.
use_for: walking every tile to read or write a whole bitmap's pixels in bulk
avoid: single-pixel reads: use Image.Pixel
cards.how: Image.Tiles, where Image is Shape.Bitmap.Image or ActiveDocument.CreateImage(...).
gotchas: the harvested member descriptions are copy-paste errors (Count says 'position of the tile's top edge'); trust the types, not the text
Item's index base is not stated; For Each avoids the question (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim t As ImageTile, n As Long
For Each t In ActiveShape.Bitmap.Image.Tiles
  n = n + t.Width * t.Height
Next t
Debug.Print n

cards.name: IVGLayer
cards.summary: A layer on a page (or the master page): its name, visibility, printability, editability and master status, the shapes on it, and the factory methods that create every kind of object (rectangles, ellipses, polygons, text, curves, bitmaps, guides, dimensions, symbols, connectors) and import files onto it.
use_for: building a whole layout from code: background, artwork and text layers
non-printing layers for notes, die-lines or guides
master layers for headers, footers and watermarks on every page
importing logos and photos onto a named layer
finding shapes by name inside a template
avoid: moving objects between layers: that is Shape.MoveToLayer, not a layer method
grouping: a layer is not a group; use Shape groups for things that move together
cards.how: ActiveLayer, ActivePage.ActiveLayer, ActivePage.Layers("name"), ActivePage.CreateLayer("name"), Shape.Layer; special layers via Page.GuidesLayer / DesktopLayer / GridLayer.

key_members.name: Master
key_members.use: master layer shown on every page

key_members.name: CreateRectangle2
key_members.use: rectangle from x, y (bottom-left), width, height and corner radii

key_members.name: CreatePolygon2
key_members.use: polygon / star from centre, radius and sides

key_members.name: CreateArtisticText
key_members.use: artistic text at left / baseline with font, size, style

key_members.name: CreateParagraphText
key_members.use: paragraph text frame from a rectangle

key_members.name: ImportEx
key_members.use: import a file and get the import filter (options, then Finish)

key_members.name: Import
key_members.use: import a file with default options

key_members.name: FindShape
key_members.use: first shape by name / type / static ID

key_members.name: FindShapes
key_members.use: all matching shapes as a ShapeRange

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: delete the layer and its shapes

gotchas: coordinates use the document unit (ActiveDocument.Unit) with the y axis pointing up from the page's bottom-left by default (unverified)
CreateRectangle takes Left, Top, Right, Bottom and corner roundness as long (a percentage, unverified), while CreateRectangle2 takes x, y, width, height and corner radii as doubles
layer loops can meet the special layers (guides, desktop, grid), e.g. over Page.AllLayers; skip them with IsSpecialLayer (which collections include them is unverified)
creating or pasting onto a layer whose Editable is False fails or lands elsewhere (unverified)
Import returns nothing; ImportEx returns the import filter so options can be set before Finish (the imported shapes are then the active selection, unverified)
Delete removes every shape on the layer with it
cards.example:
Dim lyr As Layer, t As Shape
Set lyr = ActivePage.CreateLayer("Headline")
lyr.CreateRectangle2 0, 0, 210, 297, 0, 0, 0, 0
Set t = lyr.CreateArtisticText(20, 250, "MONSOON SALE", , , "Arial", 48)
t.Name = "headline"
lyr.Printable = True

review.changes: Printable no longer claims to control export; CreateRectangle "percent" marked unverified; special-layer loop gotcha hedged; ImportEx no longer claimed to return the imported shapes (it returns ICorelImportFilter)

cards.name: IVGLayers
cards.summary: The layers of a page (or spread): Count, lookup by index or name, Find by name, For Each, and the top and bottom layers of the stack.
use_for: finding a template's named layer ("Text", "Background") before filling it
looping every layer to hide, lock or make non-printing
reading the stacking order
avoid: creating a layer: that is Page.CreateLayer
reordering: use Layer.MoveAbove / MoveBelow
cards.how: ActivePage.Layers (page layers) or ActivePage.AllLayers (also master layers); Spread.Layers / AllLayers on a spread.
gotchas: Page.Layers and Page.AllLayers differ: AllLayers also lists the master layers (guides, desktop, grid and shared master layers) (unverified)
Item by a missing name raises an error; Find returns Nothing (unverified)
the index order of Item relative to the stacking order is not stated; use Top / Bottom and Layer.Above / Below (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim lyr As Layer
For Each lyr In ActivePage.AllLayers
  If Not lyr.IsSpecialLayer Then Debug.Print lyr.Name, lyr.Visible, lyr.Printable
Next lyr
Set lyr = ActivePage.Layers.Find("Text")

cards.name: IVGLocalizableString
cards.summary: A text value stored in several languages at once (used for fill and document metadata such as title, keywords, copyright): get and set the default string or the string for a given language, and list or clear the languages present.
use_for: writing English and Hindi titles / keywords into fill or document metadata
reading metadata text in the user's language with a fallback
avoid: plain text in the artwork: that is a text Shape, not this object
cards.how: Not created on its own: it is a property of FillMetadata (Title, Description, Keywords, Subject, Copyright, Category) and of Document metadata (LocalizableTitle, LocalizableKeywords, LocalizableNotes and similar).

key_members.name: SetLangString
key_members.use: set the text for one language

key_members.name: GetLangString
key_members.use: text for one language, falling back to default or any language

key_members.name: HasLangString
key_members.use: is there text for this language

key_members.name: GetLanguages
key_members.use: array of languages that have text

key_members.name: HasDefaultLangStringOnly
key_members.use: only a default string is set

key_members.name: HasNonDefaultLangStrings
key_members.use: there are other languages besides the default

gotchas: the language code format CorelDRAW expects ("en-US", "EN", a three-letter code) is not in the harvest; read GetLanguages from an existing value first (unverified)
GetLangString silently falls back to the default or another language, so it never tells you a translation is missing; check HasLangString
IsEmpty's harvested description ('True if there is at least language string set') reads inverted; treat True as empty (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim md As FillMetadata
Set md = CreateFillMetadata
md.Title.DefaultLangString = "Festival gradient"
Debug.Print md.Title.IsEmpty, md.Title.HasDefaultLangStringOnly

cards.name: IVGMathUtils
cards.summary: Geometry helper object: creates points, vectors, point ranges and transform matrices (identity, rotation, translation, scale, segment-to-segment), and computes interpolation, midpoints, line intersections, distances, closest points, best-fit lines and random numbers.
use_for: placing objects along a line or between two anchors (Interpolate, MidPoint)
radial and rotated layouts with rotation matrices applied through Shape.ApplyTransformMatrix
snapping a label to the nearest point of a leader line
randomised confetti / pattern scatter with GetRandomReal
avoid: curve-level geometry (offsets, booleans, path lengths): use Curve and Shape methods instead
cards.how: Application.Math or ActiveDocument.Math. Points come from CreatePoint(x, y); matrices are applied with Shape.ApplyTransformMatrix.

key_members.name: Interpolate
key_members.use: point at fraction t between S and E

key_members.name: IntersectLineSegments
key_members.use: intersection of two segments; True if they cross, the point comes back through ByRef ppVal

key_members.name: DistanceToLineSegment
key_members.use: distance from a point to a segment

key_members.name: DistanceToInfiniteLine
key_members.use: distance from a point to an infinite line

key_members.name: ClosestPointToInfiniteLine
key_members.use: nearest point on an infinite line

key_members.name: FitLineToPoints
key_members.use: best-fit line (origin + direction) through a point range

key_members.name: GetRandomReal
key_members.use: random double between low and high

key_members.name: GetRandomInteger
key_members.use: random integer between low and high

key_members.name: CreateRotationTransformMatrix
key_members.use: rotation matrix about an optional origin

key_members.name: CreateScaleTransformMatrix
key_members.use: scale matrix about an optional origin

key_members.name: CreateLineSegmentTransformMatrix
key_members.use: matrix that maps one segment onto another

gotchas: the Intersect* methods return True / False and hand the intersection back through the ByRef ppVal argument (pass a Point variable; the method sets it); from Python (pywin32) the ByRef values come back as the call's returned tuple, not in the arguments (unverified)
DistanceToLineSegment and ClosestPointToLineSegment fall back to the nearest endpoint when the perpendicular misses the segment
rotation Angle is in degrees and origins in document units (unverified)
FitLineToPoints returns through its ByRef Origin and Direction arguments; from Python (pywin32) the ByRef values come back as the call's returned tuple, not in the arguments (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim m As MathUtils, s As Shape, i As Long
Set m = ActiveDocument.Math
Set s = ActiveShape
For i = 1 To 5
  s.Duplicate.ApplyTransformMatrix m.CreateRotationTransformMatrix(i * 60, s.CenterX, s.CenterY)
Next i

review.changes: Intersect* gotcha said ppVal must be pre-created with CreatePoint; it is a ByRef out pointer the method sets, now described that way and hedged for Python
